title: The Early Bird Reward minted 120% of its estimate and burns the remainder rather than sizing the mint exactly
content:
A.5.3.1.1.1 records that 27,222,832.8 newly minted SKY — 120% of total estimated Early Bird Reward distributions — was transferred to the Accessibility Facilitators' multisig, and that SKY not used to fund the MerkleDistributor will be burned by calling `burn`. The estimate needed was 22,685,694.

The pattern is over-provision-then-burn. A Merkle distribution must be fully funded before claims open, because a shortfall mid-distribution is far more damaging than a surplus: some holders simply cannot claim. Minting a 20% buffer converts an unbounded correctness risk into a bounded, reversible excess.

Burning is what makes it safe — the buffer is not retained as discretionary treasury, so the over-mint cannot quietly become spending power.
description: 27,222,832.8 SKY was minted against an estimated 22,685,694 needed, with the excess burned from the multisig — over-provision-then-burn avoids a shortfall mid-distribution.
